purpose: Test whether explicit source face-proportion diversity improves Mira identity conversion; effect not yet verified.
generation_direction: fixed Mira target -> varied non-Mira input
training_direction: reviewed non-Mira input -> original Mira target
review_checks: Input facial proportions must visibly differ from the original Mira target; a change of hair color alone is insufficient.
Assess facial length, cheek width, jaw and chin shape separately from hair volume; do not infer hidden skull shape.
Preserve head rotation, gaze, expression and mouth openness, camera, framing, body scale, pose, hands and clothing design.
Preserve background objects and their positions; reject missing or replaced objects even if the style changes.
Do not stretch the full image or change camera perspective to imitate a different face ratio.
Review each original target for Mira identity consistency before accepting any derived pair.
Keep all derivatives of the same target in its reserved split. Never automatically add generated candidates to training.
split_policy: All 15 target groups are reserved for training; keep every derivative of a target in the same split. Existing shared target train assignments are preserved. External camera evaluation remains separate.
evaluation_policy: The 45 external camera inputs and their LoRA outputs are not generation references or training targets.
